name: Hawaii: Honolulu, North Shore, Kihei, Hana, West Maui

cities.base: Waikiki's east end on the Kapahulu side: Rainbow, Leonard's and Ono Seafood are 5 to 15 minutes' walk. Add $30 to $50 a day each for resort fees and parking.
cities.name: Honolulu

cities.base: Haleiwa town, where the shrimp trucks and shops are. No mid-range hotel was sourced; $363 is the Other Oahu average, and the drive time from Honolulu is unverified.
cities.name: The North Shore (Haleiwa)

cities.base: South Kihei Rd between Kamaole parks I and III, all the food within 2 km. $734 is the Wailea hotel average; Kihei runs lower but no rate was found. 46 min flight HNL to OGG.
cities.name: Kihei and Wailea

cities.base: Hana town near the bay, with the lunch trucks on Hana Hwy. No room rate was found, so price it before you plan on it. Fly to OGG, then drive the Road to Hana.
cities.name: Hana and East Maui

cities.base: Sleep in Kaanapali or Napili, $410 average. Lahaina is a recovering town and a day visit for now: residents first, stay out of fenced areas.
cities.name: Lahaina and West Maui

places.name: Rainbow Drive-In
places.note: Plate lunch counter since 1961: order the chili dog plate ($12.95), two scoops rice and mac salad. Happy hour Mon to Thu 15:00 to 17:00 knocks the chili plate to $10 and the loco moco to $12, no alcohol.

places.name: Helena's Hawaiian Food
places.note: Order the pipikaula short ribs and lomi salmon, or the $19.50 pipikaula combo plate. Cash or personal check, closed Saturday, Sunday and Monday, and the kitchen stops about 30 minutes before closing, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Leonard's Bakery
places.note: Hot malasadas at $1.50 to $2.50 each, plain or filled with custard, haupia, guava or li hing; a few pieces is $6 to $10. The queue is long and it moves.

places.name: Liliha Bakery
places.note: Counter breakfast since 1950: three hot cakes $12.50 and a coco puff ($2.19), the chocolate pudding puff with cream on top. Prices are from an undated menu.

places.name: Side Street Inn on Hopaka
places.note: Where locals go for pupu and the pork chop; a 2026 bill ran $120 for two with three entrees and a drink each. Closed Monday, lunch on weekends from 12:00, valet $8.

places.name: Ono Seafood
places.note: Tiny poke counter: a bowl is about $16 for 5 oz or $18 for 8 oz. Closed Sunday and Monday, and it shuts at 16:00, so make it lunch.

places.name: Iolani Palace
places.note: The palace of the Hawaiian monarchy, now a history museum with docent tours. Admission was not confirmed, so check the price at iolanipalace.org and book ahead. Closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Bishop Museum
places.note: The state's big Hawaiian and Pacific museum; Hawaiian Hall is the gallery to give your time to. About $35 adult (converted from a euro listing), open daily, the best rainy day on Oahu.

places.name: Honolulu Museum of Art
places.note: The island's art museum, $25 adult, with a cafe for lunch. Closed Monday and Tuesday; Friday it stays open to 21:00.

places.name: Kawaiahao Church
places.note: Historic church on the downtown walk with Iolani Palace. Visiting hours run longer on weekdays and services can close it, so hours vary, check; a $26.25 ticket is listed, likely a guided tour, so check the price.

places.name: Queen Emma Summer Palace
places.note: The royal summer retreat in the cool of Nuuanu valley, kept as a historic house museum; $18.75 adult. Closed Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, and it shuts at 15:00.

places.name: Capitol Modern: Hawaii State Art Museum
places.note: Free state art museum on the second floor, next to Iolani Palace, so it slots into the downtown walk. Closed Sunday, Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: Foster Botanical Garden
places.note: An hour of shade at the edge of Chinatown for $5 adult. Go first thing, before the downtown heat.

places.name: Hawaiian Mission Houses Historic Site
places.note: Historic missionary houses and archive across from Kawaiahao Church; about $10 adult (converted from a euro listing), so confirm at missionhouses.org. Closed Sunday and Monday, shuts at 15:00.

places.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial and USS Arizona Memorial
places.note: Free, but book the Memorial program on Recreation.gov ($1 a ticket): releases at 15:00 HST 8 weeks and 24 hours ahead. Programs every 15 minutes from 08:00, arrive an hour early, and dock repairs can cancel them.

places.name: Diamond Head State Monument (Leahi)
places.note: Trail built in 1908 for Oahu's coastal defense: 0.8 mi and 560 ft up through a lit 225 ft tunnel to the bunkers. Non-residents must reserve at gostateparks.hawaii.gov, $5 on foot, card only, last entry 16:30.

places.name: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck
places.note: The garlic shrimp plate, $17.50 in 2026 against $14 in 2021. Bring cash for the $2 parking and expect the longest line on the strip.

places.name: Big Wave Shrimp
places.note: Same strip as Giovanni's, about $17 to $20 a plate in 2026, and the reason to pick it is the shorter line. Open to 18:30, later than its neighbour.

places.name: Kua Aina Sandwich Shop
places.note: Burger and sandwich shop; the eggplant and peppers sandwich was $13 in late 2025. Closed Tuesday, and open to 20:00 on weekends.

places.name: Waialua Bakery & Juice Bar
places.note: Lunch and baked goods, rated 4.8 on Google; the chicken pesto sandwich was $12 in August 2026. Closed Sunday, shuts at 16:00.

places.name: Haleiwa Beach House
places.note: The evening drink in Haleiwa, on the water. Reviewers call it pricey and no menu prices were found, so check the price. Closed Tuesday.

places.name: Puu o Mahuka Heiau State Historic Site
places.note: A heiau, a Hawaiian temple site, on the bluff above Waimea Bay; free. Closed Sunday, and one visitor reports the gate opening at 07:00, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Waimea Valley
places.note: Botanical garden and cultural center with a path to Waimea Falls, rated 4.6 from 9,142 reviews. Entry was not listed, so check the price.

places.name: Haleiwa Historic Town
places.note: The shops and galleries strung along Kamehameha Hwy, free to walk; pair it with a shrimp truck lunch. Shops keep roughly 10:00 to 17:30.

places.name: Laniakea Beach
places.note: Free beach on the Kamehameha Hwy between Haleiwa and Waimea, rated 4.7 from 5,895 reviews. Parking along the road is the thing that goes wrong.

places.name: Shark's Cove
places.note: Rocky cove at Pupukea, free, a short drive past Waimea Bay. Go in the morning before the parking fills.

places.name: Waimea Bay
places.note: The North Shore's famous bay, free, rated 4.8 on Google; pair it with Puu o Mahuka heiau on the bluff above.

places.name: Ehukai Pillbox Trail
places.note: Free hike up to the pillboxes above Sunset Beach and Banzai; trail length was not stated, allow an hour.

places.name: Sunset Beach Park
places.note: Long free beach at the east end of the North Shore, rated 4.7 from 2,438 reviews; end a day here for the light.

places.name: Kaena Point State Park
places.note: Oahu's far western tip, free, rated 4.8; trail length was not stated, so allow three hours and carry water. Gates 06:00 to 18:45.

places.name: Kihei Caffe
places.note: Breakfast institution: loco moco $19.95, pancakes or an omelette $12.95. The queue between 07:00 and 09:00 is the problem, so go at opening.

places.name: Coconuts Fish Cafe
places.note: Order the fish tacos ($20); mahi fish and chips is $21. Counter service in the Azeka center, open daily 11:00 to 21:00.

places.name: Nalu's South Shore Grill
places.note: Loco moco $16 to $17, burgers $17 to $19, the poke bowl of the day $25. Those are lunch prices; dinner was not seen.

places.name: Maui Brewing Co. Kihei
places.note: The brewery's big Kihei taproom for an evening beer; opens 09:00 at weekends. No menu prices were found, so check the price.

places.name: Bailey House Museum (Maui Historical Society)
places.note: Maui Historical Society museum in Wailuku, about 25 minutes north of Kihei; a visitor paid $10. Open Tuesday to Friday 10:00 to 14:00, closed Saturday, Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Iao Valley State Monument
places.note: The valley and the Iao Needle Lookout Trail; paid reservations are required, about $16.40 plus parking on the booking page. Go early, before cloud fills the valley head.

places.name: Alexander & Baldwin Sugar Museum
places.note: Plantation-era sugar history, with the mill next door; $12 adult. Open Monday to Thursday, last admission 13:00, closed Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

places.name: Kaahumanu Church
places.note: Historic church a block from the Bailey House in Wailuku, free. Visiting hours were not reliable on any page, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Kepaniwai Park
places.note: Free heritage park and gardens on the road up to Iao Valley; stop on the way in.

places.name: Humpback Whale National Marine Sanctuary Visitor Center
places.note: Free visitor center on the Kihei shore with free parking. Weekdays 09:30 to 14:30, closed Saturday and Sunday.

places.name: Kealia Pond National Wildlife Refuge
places.note: Free coastal boardwalk over the wetland bird refuge between Kihei and Maalaea; the cloudy-morning plan.

places.name: Wailea Beach
places.note: The resort beach of Wailea, free and public, rated 4.7. Public hours 07:00 to 20:00.

places.name: Keawakapu Beach
places.note: Free beach between Kihei and Wailea, rated 4.8 from 1,006 reviews; quieter than Wailea Beach.

places.name: Polo Beach
places.note: Small free beach at the south end of Wailea, rated 4.7; the one to pick when Wailea Beach is full.

places.name: Braddah Hutt's BBQ Grill
places.note: Food truck: kalua pork $15, mahi $17, BBQ ribs $16 on an undated listing. Closed Saturday and Sunday, lunch only.

places.name: Thai Food by Pranee
places.note: Thai lunch stand at $10 to $16 a plate (undated guide). Closed Thursday, and the guide's hours are shorter than Google's, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Da Fish Shack
places.note: Fish plates at $14 to $16 (undated guide). Sources disagree on which midweek days it shuts, so hours vary, check before you drive over.

places.name: Hana Ranch Restaurant
places.note: The one sit-down dinner in town, mains $12 to $32 (undated guide). Open daily to 20:30, so it is the plan for the night you sleep in Hana.

places.name: Hana Farms Roadside Stand & Restaurant
places.note: Farm stand with a grill; order the fish tacos, about $15 to $20 a meal, cards taken. The stand keeps longer hours than the grill, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Waianapanapa State Park
places.note: Black sand at Pailoa, a sea arch, blowholes, a heiau and the coast trail. Reserve entry and parking first: $5 a person plus $10 a car. A 2026 park notice has contradictory reopening dates, so check the notices.

places.name: Kahanu Garden and Piilanihale Heiau
places.note: Piilanihale Heiau: a 14th-century temple of five basalt terraces, 341 by 415 ft with a 50 ft front wall, enlarged in the 16th century. An admission fee is charged, so check the price; hours vary, check (808 248 8912).

places.name: Hana Bay
places.note: The town's bay and beach park, free, five minutes from every lunch truck; the place to sit after the drive in.

places.name: Aloha Mixed Plate
places.note: Back on the reopened Front Street: kalbi, chicken katsu, or kalua pig with lomi salmon, about $20 to $25 an entree. Happy hour 14:00 to 16:30. Booking sites show longer hours, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Mala Ocean Tavern
places.note: Oceanfront, closed by the fire on 8 Aug 2023 and reopened 1 Feb 2024. Brunch runs 08:00 to 14:00 with $7 mimosas and is the better value; dinner entrees go upwards of $45.

places.name: Honu Oceanside
places.note: Reopened October 2024 after more than a year shut, on the north end of Front Street that is open again. Dinner from 16:30, $17 to $47 a main on an undated guide.

places.name: Maui Brewing Co. Kaanapali
places.note: The Kaanapali taproom, open 07:00 to 22:00 daily, for a beer near the beds. No menu prices were found, so check the price.

places.name: Kapalua Coastal Trail
places.note: Paved, easy, free path between Kapalua Bay Beach and D.T. Fleming Beach Park, rated 4.8. Do it early, before the heat.

places.name: Napili Bay
places.note: Free crescent bay at Napili, rated 4.8; a good reason to sleep at this end of the coast.

places.name: Honolua Bay
places.note: Free bay north of Kapalua, rated 4.8 from 412 reviews; go in the morning when the water is calmest.

places.name: Kaanapali Beach
places.note: The long resort beach in front of the hotels, free and public. Kaanapali's resorts are fully operating, so this is the easy bed on the west side.

places.name: Maria Lanakila Catholic Church
places.note: Catholic church in Lahaina, free, rated 4.8. Whether it is open to visitors since the fire is not confirmed, so treat it as a look from outside.

places.name: Lahaina Banyan Tree
places.note: Survived the 2023 fire and is putting out new growth. Sources conflict on whether the park is open, so do not count on walking under it; look from Front Street and stay out of fenced areas.
places.neighborhood: Lahaina, Front St and Canal St

outings.why: Entry 3:00 to 7:00 AM needs a $1 Recreation.gov ticket per car, mostly released 60 days ahead at 7 a.m. HST, some 48 hours ahead; no walk-ups. Park fee $30 a car on top. 30 to 50 F colder than the coast.
outings.name: Haleakala summit for sunrise
outings.fallback: On a cloudy morning, Iao Valley and the Bailey House in Wailuku, or the Kealia Pond boardwalk.

outings.why: Book Waianapanapa entry and parking ahead ($5 a person, $10 a car, 07:00 to 18:00). Kipahulu is 12 miles past Hana: the Oheo pools are closed to entry, seen from the Kuloa Point Trail. Drive time unverified.
outings.name: The Road to Hana and Waianapanapa
outings.fallback: Wailuku and Iao Valley with the Kihei sights; check Hawaii DOT road status before leaving.

destination.name: Hawaii: Honolulu, North Shore, Kihei, Hana, West Maui
destination.pitch: Two islands in a week to ten days: Honolulu for Pearl Harbor, the palace and plate lunch, a few nights on the North Shore, then fly to Maui for Kihei, a night in Hana and the Haleakala sunrise. Book the reservations first.
destination.caveat: Book ahead: Pearl Harbor, Diamond Head, Iao Valley, Waianapanapa and the Haleakala sunrise. Rooms are dear ($410 West Maui, $734 Wailea). Lahaina is recovering from the 2023 fire; Front Street reopened to cars in August 2026, but its museums and historic sites are closed or unconfirmed. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Honolulu carries the city part: a downtown walk of Iolani Palace, Kawaiahao Church, the Mission Houses and Capitol Modern, all within a few blocks.
because.food: Plate lunch at Rainbow, Hawaiian food at Helena's, malasadas at Leonard's, poke at Ono, garlic shrimp in Haleiwa, fish tacos at Coconuts in Kihei.
because.nature: Diamond Head, Kaena Point and Waimea Valley on Oahu; Iao Valley, Waianapanapa's black sand and the Haleakala summit on Maui.
because.culture: Iolani Palace, Queen Emma Summer Palace, the Bishop Museum and Pearl Harbor in Honolulu, then the Sugar Museum and Bailey House on Maui and Piilanihale Heiau, a 14th-century temple, near Hana.
because.relaxation: Napili Bay and Kaanapali on the west side, Wailea, Keawakapu and Polo in the south, Sunset Beach and Waimea Bay on Oahu.
